initial_inventory.title: [Kernel][SM70] Generalise the MXFP4 MoE geometry and add skinny split-K 4/6/9/12/18

metadata.title: [Kernel][SM70] Generalise the MXFP4 MoE geometry and add skinny split-K 4/6/9/12/18
metadata.body:
> Contributed by PLI Labs (Proprietary Legal Intelligence). The same branch is published at [ProprietaryLegal/1Cat-vLLM](https://github.com/ProprietaryLegal/1Cat-vLLM/tree/feat/sm70-mxfp4-moe-geometry). It is the first piece of the DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash port to V100 (#1031; patches and results at [ProprietaryLegal/deepseek-v4.1-flash-sm70](https://huggingface.co/ProprietaryLegal/deepseek-v4.1-flash-sm70)).

## Purpose

Today the SM70 MXFP4 MoE path accepts exactly one expert geometry: DeepSeek-V4-Flash's, with hidden 4096, intermediate 2048, 256 experts and top-6. Those constants are also baked into the buffers, the active-expert compaction and the stage dispatch. On top of that, the grouped skinny kernel has only split-K 8, 10 and 16 and requires K % 64, so a down projection with K = 576 or K = 288 has no admitted split.

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash keeps V4's MXFP4 byte format but changes the geometry:
- hidden 5120 and intermediate 2304 (576 per rank at TP4, 288 at TP8);
- 384 experts top-6 in the backbone, and 128 experts top-3 in the DSpark draft layers.

This PR generalises the path for those shapes. DeepSeek-V4-Flash keeps exactly the kernels and paths it uses today.

## Changes

1. **`skinny_moe_qpn_sm70`.**
   - New split-K specialisations 4, 6, 9, 12 and 18, with one accumulator. They cover K/16 = 36 and K/16 = 18.
   - The grouped op now checks K % 32, which is what it actually needs: it walks K in 16-code groups and reads one MXFP4 scale per pair of groups. The dense QPN GEMM keeps K % 64.
   - Python exposes the new cases through `grouped_splitk(..., extended=True)` and `qpn_prepack(..., k_align=32)`. Both default to today's behaviour, so the skinny backend admission and the chosen split are unchanged for every existing caller.
2. **`Mxfp4SM70MoEMethod`.**
   - The contract is keyed on (hidden, intermediate), with the admitted (experts, top-k) pairs listed per geometry. The V4-Flash refusal messages keep their wording.
   - top-k and hidden size are taken from the layer.
   - The V4-Flash-only fused decode paths (direct top-6, compact and broadcast grouped decode, QPN M1) are gated on the exact V4-Flash geometry (`_v4_flash_fast_paths`). Every other admitted geometry runs the generic permute + grouped stages, now shared through `_generic_stages`.
   - New `apply_slots()` returns the unweighted per-route expert outputs in route order. It serves callers that combine routes themselves, for example in FP32 with a shared expert.

Diff: 4 files, +657 / −140, of which 378 lines are the new test file.

## Test Plan

```console
# build _C for TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST=7.0, then
pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_sm70_mxfp4_moe_geometry.py tests/quantization/test_sm70_mxfp4_moe.py \
       tests/kernels/moe/test_skinny_sm70_moe.py
```

`tests/kernels/moe/test_sm70_mxfp4_moe_geometry.py` (new, self-contained) covers:
- **Contract.** Admission of the 4 qualified geometries and 7 refusals. These run on CPU.
- **V4-Flash.** At TP4 and TP8 with T = 1/2/8/33, the fast paths are still selected, `apply` matches an FP32 dequantised reference (rel-RMS < 2e-3), and `apply_slots` combined equals `apply`.
- **V4.1 geometries.** 384 × top-6 and 128 × top-3 at TP4 with T = 1/3/17 run on the generic stages and match the reference.
- **Skinny admission.** Unchanged for existing callers; the `k_align` check works.
- **New splits.** They agree with the old ones on the old shapes. At K = 576 and K = 288 they match the FP32 reference (rel-RMS < 1e-3).

## Test Result

Hardware: one V100-SXM2-32GB (SM clock 1477 MHz). Driver 580.159.03, CUDA 12.8.93, torch 2.10.0+cu128. `_C` was built from this branch on main `3d56d9910`.

- **New test file:** 21/21 pass.
- **Existing suites** `tests/quantization/test_sm70_mxfp4_moe.py` and `tests/kernels/moe/test_skinny_sm70_moe.py`: 116 passed, 13 skipped, and 2 failed. Both also fail on main (recorded on `2d5078372` by our build smoke): `test_mxfp4_sm70_factory_selects_native_route` and `test_mxfp4_sm70_factory_rejects_marlin_or_emulation`. Both predate this change; since 1Cat `0bce84469` routed V4 MXFP4 experts to the skinny backend, these tests expect the old route.
- **Full DeepSeek-V4.1 model.** These exact Python and CUDA sources are part of the V4.1 stack that passed its end-to-end checks on 8 and 12 V100s. On real V4.1 layers (3, 10, 29 and the MTP layer, TP4 and TP1, T = 1…4096), MoE rel-RMS against FP32 was 3.5e-4…4.3e-4 and router top-6 agreed 100 %.
- **V4-Flash regression in the V4.1 work.** The bitwise skinny snapshot over 416 cases showed 0 mismatches against the pre-change build.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

https://claude.ai/code/session_01MsmVmETN2WsrLJg2uGM183
